summary: Addressing class imbalance does not meaningfully improve model quality on this dataset. Cross-validated ROC-AUC scores show minimal differences between baseline models and imbalance-handling approaches (Δ ≤ 0.003), with the baseline RandomForest performing comparably to or better than weighted, SMOTE, or undersampled variants. The 3.18:1 class imbalance ratio is not severe enough to warrant intervention, and tree-based models are naturally robust to this degree of imbalance.
direction: No meaningful difference; imbalance handling slightly degrades or has negligible effect
methodological_choices: Model: RandomForest (n_estimators=100, max_depth=20) as primary learner, validated with LogisticRegression. Imbalance handling methods: class weights (balanced), SMOTE, random undersampling. Preprocessing: LabelEncoder for categorical features, StandardScaler for numeric features. Train-test split: 80-20 stratified split (random_state=42). Evaluation metric: ROC-AUC (primary) and F1-Score (secondary). Validation: 5-fold stratified cross-validation repeated with 3 different random seeds (42, 123, 456) for stability assessment.
verification_method: 5-fold stratified cross-validation repeated with 3 random seeds (15 total folds per approach). Evaluated both RandomForest and LogisticRegression across four imbalance-handling strategies: (1) baseline (no handling), (2) class weights, (3) SMOTE, (4) random undersampling. Assessed consistency by examining min/max/range of fold scores and proportion of folds where imbalance-handling outperformed baseline.
verification_result: Finding held up under cross-validation. Best-performing imbalance approach (Weighted RF: 0.9162±0.0025 ROC-AUC) performed virtually identically to baseline (0.9164±0.0024). Other approaches (SMOTE: 0.9125±0.0026, Undersampling: 0.9139±0.0024) showed consistent degradation. Baseline outperformed in 10 of 15 folds. The negligible difference (-0.0002) persisted across all random seeds, confirming that addressing imbalance provides no benefit on this dataset.
